channel.title: Money Math Daily
channel.description: The math behind everyday money decisions, worked out step by step.

item.title: APR vs APY, What the Difference Means in Dollars
item.description: APR and APY sound alike but answer different questions. See how each is defined in federal rules and what the gap is worth on savings and card balances.

item.title: How Investment Fees Compound Over Time, With the Math
item.description: A 1% fee sounds tiny, but it is charged every year on a growing balance. Here is how ongoing fees reduce long-term results, using federal examples.

item.title: Inflation, Explained With a Grocery Receipt
item.description: How the Consumer Price Index measures rising prices, illustrated with a simple grocery cart example and the math behind purchasing power loss.

item.title: The Rule of 72, and Where It Actually Breaks Down
item.description: A plain explanation of the Rule of 72 shortcut for doubling time, with the real math showing exactly how far off it gets at higher rates.

item.title: What a Credit Card's Minimum Payment Really Costs You
item.description: The federal rule behind the minimum payment warning on your statement, and a worked example showing how much extra time and interest it adds.

item.title: What Saving $100 a Month Really Adds Up To
item.description: A plain-numbers look at how $100 saved monthly grows over 10, 20, 30, and 40 years under one assumed, clearly stated rate of return.
